spec: the keyed sender mapping, its whole-channel refusal, and payload.sender.hashed (APRV-370)

Three amendments, all additive and all describing what the commit before this
one implements.

§5.2 gains the KEYED form of a `senders` value beside the raw account id, the
rule that a plain unkeyed digest MUST NOT be offered for this purpose (a
transport account id is a short number and the space is enumerable), that the
form is per entry so one policy may carry a migration in progress, and that a
channel with any keyed entry and no key in the deciding process MUST refuse
every decision on it without falling back to the raw entries. It says plainly
that the key authenticates nothing and that an implementation MUST NOT present
losing it as a loss of safety.

§6.3/§10.3 gains `payload.sender.hashed`, present-and-`true` or absent and never
`false`, and the rule that the digest recorded is the value the MATCHED entry
carries, so a log correlates to a policy without the reader holding the key.

The §11.2 refusal table gains the `sender-key-unavailable` row, including why it
refuses the whole channel rather than its keyed half and why the record it
writes carries the raw id: there is no key to hash it with, and a record naming
no account would leave an operator unable to say who was in front of a gate that
had lost its key.
